container: Overpopulation creates challenges for communities and governments. When population growth exceeds resources, housing becomes scarce, prices rise, and many families live in crowded or unsafe conditions. Schools and hospitals struggle to serve everyone, while roads and public transport become congested. Greater demand for food and water can worsen shortages and damage ecosystems. More waste and pollution threaten public health and contribute to climate change. Overpopulation may also increase unemployment and deepen poverty, especially where opportunities are limited. Addressing these pressures requires education, voluntary family planning, sustainable cities, and fair resource distribution so people can thrive.
